# SmartDns — full reference for language models

SmartDns is a single-purpose Node.js library: it resolves hostnames to IP addresses and
caches the result so the same question is not asked twice. It is a zero-runtime-dependency
TypeScript package published as @darcas/smart-dns-promises under the MIT license.

Source: [GitHub repository](https://github.com/DarCas/smart-dns-promises)
Package: [npm @darcas/smart-dns-promises](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@darcas/smart-dns-promises)
Website: [smartdns.os.darcas.app](https://smartdns.os.darcas.app/)

## Positioning

"The route before the request." DNS resolution happens before a connection is opened, so it
is invisible in application telemetry yet repeated on every call. SmartDns keeps resolved
hostnames in a TTL-aware cache, collapses concurrent lookups for the same host, and only
contacts the resolver when it has to.

SmartDns does not replace the HTTP client. It resolves the hostname first, then the client
sends the request to the resolved address, keeping the original hostname in the Host header.

## Requirements

- Node.js 20 or >= 22 (engines: "20 || >= 22")
- No runtime dependencies
- TypeScript types included; ships both ESM and CJS entry points

## Installation

    npm install @darcas/smart-dns-promises

## Quick start

    import { SmartDns, DnsProvider } from '@darcas/smart-dns-promises'

    const dns = SmartDns.factory(DnsProvider.CloudFlare)

    const { address, hostname, urlReplaced } =
        await dns.resolver('https://www.google.com')

    // address     -> '142.250.72.14'
    // hostname    -> 'www.google.com'
    // urlReplaced -> 'https://142.250.72.14/'

## Public API

### DnsProvider

Numeric enum: AdGuard, CloudFlare, Comodo, DnsWatch, Google, OpenDNS, Quad9, Verisign, Yandex.

### SmartDns.factory(dnsProvider?, resultOrder?, ttl?, options?)

Returns the singleton resolver. Configuration passed after the first call is ignored, so
initialize it early. ttl (milliseconds) is the fallback lifetime used only when a DNS record
reports no TTL.

resultOrder: 'ipv4first' | 'ipv6first' | 'verbatim'.

### dns.resolver(url)

    async resolver(url: string): Promise<{ address: IPAddress; hostname: Hostname; urlReplaced: string }>

Accepts absolute http/https URLs. Throws SmartDnsResolverError for an invalid URL or a
negative-cached hostname.

### dns.setProvider(dnsProvider)

Selects the upstream resolver:
- AdGuard: 94.140.14.14, 94.140.15.15
- CloudFlare: 1.1.1.1, 1.0.0.1
- Comodo: 8.26.56.26, 8.20.247.20
- DnsWatch: 84.200.69.80, 84.200.70.40
- Google: 8.8.8.8, 8.8.4.4
- OpenDNS: 208.67.222.222, 208.67.220.220
- Quad9: 9.9.9.9, 149.112.112.112
- Verisign: 64.6.64.6, 64.6.65.6
- Yandex: 77.88.8.8, 77.88.8.1

An unknown provider throws SmartDnsProviderError.

### dns.setServers(servers)

    dns.setServers(['9.9.9.9', '149.112.112.112'])

### dns.stats

    { hits, misses, errors, revalidations, avgResolveMs }

avgResolveMs is the total resolve time divided by the number of real resolutions, and is 0
when no resolution has happened yet.

### Options

    SmartDns.factory(DnsProvider.CloudFlare, 'ipv4first', 3_600_000, {
        family: 'ipv4',
        minTtl: 1_000,
        maxTtl: 3_600_000,
        negativeTtl: 30_000,
        swr: true,
        onStats: (stats) => console.log(stats)
    })

- family: 'ipv4' | 'ipv6' (default 'ipv4')
- minTtl / maxTtl: clamp the effective lifetime of a cached record
- negativeTtl: lifetime of the negative cache
- swr: serve stale entries while revalidating in the background
- onStats: called with the updated statistics

## Resolution order

1. A valid cached entry is returned immediately (hit).
2. If SWR is enabled, an expired entry is served immediately and refreshed in the background.
3. A recently failed hostname is rejected from the negative cache.
4. Only here is a DNS query issued. The answer is cached respecting the record TTL.

## Integrations

### Axios

    import axios from 'axios'
    import { SmartDns, DnsProvider } from '@darcas/smart-dns-promises'

    const dns = SmartDns.factory(DnsProvider.OpenDNS)

    axios.interceptors.request.use(async (config) => {
        const { hostname, urlReplaced } = await dns.resolver(config.url!)

        config.headers.Host = hostname
        config.url = urlReplaced
        return config
    })

### Fetch

    const { hostname, urlReplaced } = await dns.resolver('http://service.internal/health')

    const response = await fetch(urlReplaced, {
        headers: { Host: hostname }
    })

Replacing the host with an IP means TLS is negotiated against that IP, so the direct fetch
approach is best suited to plain HTTP and controlled environments; prefer the interceptor for
public HTTPS.

## Process-wide behavior

setProvider, setServers and Node's result ordering are process-global. Every HTTP client in
the process, including third-party dependencies, inherits the same resolution strategy. This
is intentional: configure DNS once and let the process use it. Initialize SmartDns early and
avoid conflicting configurations.

## Errors

- SmartDnsProviderError: unknown or unsupported DNS provider.
- SmartDnsResolverError: invalid URL, or a hostname held in the negative cache.

## Performance language

SmartDns avoids unnecessary DNS work and keeps repeated lookups out of the critical path. It
does not claim absolute speedups; the actual benefit depends on the workload and how often the
same hostnames are resolved.
